# Get-ZbxError

## SYNOPSIS

Gets recent Zabbix failures from the engine's own $Error, newest first.

## SYNTAX

### Recent (Default)

```
Get-ZbxError [[-Last] <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### All

```
Get-ZbxError -AllErrors [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Every failure this module writes is an ErrorRecord whose FullyQualifiedErrorId starts with Zabbix and names its kind (ZabbixApi.PermissionOrNotFound, ZabbixWire.ConnectionRefused). This command reads the session's own $Error and writes the records a command of the Community.Zabbix modules wrote (the engine's own binding errors for those commands included) or that carry an exception from the Zabbix libraries, newest first: the last 16 by default, -Last N, or all of them with -AllErrors. It keeps no log of its own, so how many are kept is $MaximumErrorCount, and $Error.Clear() clears them.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: See the failures a script caught

```powershell
'web-98', 'web-99' | ForEach-Object {
    try { Remove-ZbxHost -InputObject $_ -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Stop } catch { Write-Warning $_ }
}
Get-ZbxError -Last 2 | Select-Object FullyQualifiedErrorId, @{ n = 'Message'; e = { $_.Exception.Message } }
```

Get-ZbxError reads the session's own $Error, keeping only the module's failures, newest first, so failures a script caught (or hid with -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) can still be looked at afterwards.

### Example 2: Tell failures apart by their error id

```powershell
'web-02', 'web-01' | ForEach-Object {
    New-ZbxHost -Host $_ -Group 'Web servers' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
} | Select-Object TechnicalName
Get-ZbxError -Last 1 | ForEach-Object {
    if ($_.FullyQualifiedErrorId -like 'ZabbixApi.*') { 'The server refused: ' + $_.Exception.Message }
    else { 'Other failure: ' + $_.Exception.Message }
}
```

Each failure's FullyQualifiedErrorId names its kind (ZabbixReferenceNotFound, ZabbixApi.Validation...), so a script can react to one kind without parsing messages. Here web-01 already exists, so the server refuses it.

### Example 3: Summarise every buffered failure

```powershell
Get-ZbxError -AllErrors | Group-Object { $_.FullyQualifiedErrorId.Split(',')[0] } | Select-Object Count, Name
```

-AllErrors reads every failure still in $Error (bounded by $MaximumErrorCount); group them by kind.
